c.tagline: Whitewashed Casbah alleys tumble to a sweeping Mediterranean bay.

taxi.fareNote: Official taxis are metered with a small starting fare plus per-km charge; agree on a price beforehand for airport or intercity trips, as meters are sometimes 'not working' for tourists.

emergency.note: Gendarmerie Nationale can also be reached at 1055; French is widely understood by responders, English less so.

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing in the Casbah and city centre; caution at night

hood_desc: The historic heart of Algiers around the UNESCO-listed Casbah and Place des Martyrs, with colonial Haussmann-style boulevards, the cheapest lodging, and easy walking access to museums and street food; suits first-time visitors and budget travelers.

An affluent, leafy hillside suburb of embassies, upscale apartments, and restaurants overlooking the bay; suits business travelers and those wanting a quiet, secure base a short taxi ride from downtown.
A cooler hilltop colonial-era quarter of villas and gardens above the city, home to the storied Hotel El Djazair; suits couples and travelers wanting atmosphere and calm away from downtown traffic.
A seafront strip of pine-lined resort and conference hotels east of downtown, anchored by the Hilton and Sheraton Club des Pins; suits business visitors and families wanting a pool or beach access.
A modern business and university district near the airport with international chain hotels and convention facilities; suits transit travelers and conference-goers prioritizing airport proximity.

water.note: Aging pipes mean tap water carries contamination risk; drink bottled water instead.

transit.pay: Metro and tram use paper tickets or rechargeable cards bought at station counters/machines and validated at gates or onboard validators; buses are typically paid in small-denomination cash to the driver or conductor. Contactless bank-card payment is not yet common on public transit.
transit.hours: Metro and tram operate roughly 5:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m.; buses run similar daytime hours with sparse or no late-night service, after which taxis are the main option.
transit.note: Network is limited to one metro line, one tram line, and buses; central Algiers and the Casbah are best explored on foot given steep, narrow streets.

train: SNTF national rail linking Algiers to Oran, Constantine, Annaba and other cities
bus: Intercity coaches from Gare Routière Caroubier
ferry: Algérie Ferries seasonal routes to Marseille and Alicante

transit.m: Airport shuttle/city bus to Grande Poste (~40-50 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% in sit-down restaurants is appreciated but rarely expected, and taxi drivers are not usually tipped.
